sanskrit: divyo gandharvo bhuvanasya yas patir ekāyuvo namasā vikṣv īḍyaḥ | taṃ tvā yaumi brahmaṇā deva divya namas te astu divi te sadhastham ||
english: The divine Gandharva who is lord of the world, worthy of praise among the peoples with obeisance by the single-lived — thee, that one, I hymn with sacred utterance, O divine god; homage be to thee; thy dwelling-place is in the sky.

sanskrit: diva spṛṣṭo yajataḥ sūryatvag avayātā haraso daivyasya | ekāyuvo namasā suśevo mṛḍād gandharvo bhuvanasya yas patiḥ ||
english: Touched by heaven, adorable, with skin of sunlight, he has driven off the fury of the divine wrath; gracious with obeisance by the single-lived — may the Gandharva, who is lord of the world, show favour.

sanskrit: anavadyābhiḥ sam u jagma ābhir apsarābhir api gandharva āsu | samudra āsāṃ sadanaṃ ma āhur yataḥ sadya ā ca parā ca yanti ||
english: The Gandharva too has indeed come together with these blameless Apsarases; they say their dwelling is the ocean, whence they go hither and thither at once.

sanskrit: abhriye didyun nakṣatriye yā viśvāvasuṃ gandharvaṃ sacadhve | tābhyo vo devīr nama it kṛṇomi ||
english: O lightning-flash of the clouds, O star-born ones, you who attend upon the Gandharva Viśvāvasu — to those of you, O goddesses, I make obeisance.

sanskrit: yāḥ klandās tamiṣīcayo akṣakāmā manomuhaḥ | tābhyo gandharvapatnībhyo apsarābhyo 'karaṃ namaḥ ||
english: Those who are weepers, dwellers in darkness, eager for dice-play, bewitchers of the mind — to those Apsarases, wives of the Gandharvas, I have paid homage.

sanskrit: amuṣmād adhi parvatād avatkam asi bheṣajam | bheṣajaṃ subheṣajaṃ yat te kṛṇomi bheṣajam ||
english: From yonder mountain thou art drawn forth as a healing remedy; a remedy, an excellent remedy — whatever remedy I make of thee.

sanskrit: ād aṅgā kuvid aṅgā śataṃ yad bheṣajāni te sahasraṃ vā gha yāni te | teṣām asi tvam uttamam anāsrāvam arogaṇam ||
english: Indeed, indeed — the hundred remedies that are thine, and the thousand that are thine: of those thou art the highest, free from leaking away, free from disease.

sanskrit: arusyānam idaṃ mahat pṛthivyā adhy udbhṛtam | tad āsrāvasya bheṣajaṃ tad u rogam anīnaśat ||
english: This great red-blooded one has been lifted up from the earth; that is the remedy against discharge, and it has indeed destroyed disease.

sanskrit: upajīkā ud bharanti samudrād adhi bheṣajam | arusyānam asy ātharvaṇaṃ rogasthānam asy ātharvaṇam ||
english: The field-crickets carry up the remedy from the ocean; thou art the Ātharvaṇa remedy for the wound, thou art the Ātharvaṇa seat-of-disease.

sanskrit: ayaṃ devānām asuro vi rājati vaśā hi satyā varuṇasya rājñaḥ | tatas pari brahmaṇā śāśadāna ugrasya manyor ud imaṃ nayāmi ||
english: This one is the Asura of the gods who rules on high — for the command of King Varuṇa is true; conquering over and beyond that with sacred utterance, I lead this man up out of the fierce wrath.

sanskrit: namas te rājan varuṇāstu manyave viśvaṃ hi deva nicikeṣi drugdham | śataṃ sahasraṃ pra suvāmy anyān ayaṃ no jīvan śarado vyāpet ||
english: Homage to thee, O King Varuṇa, to thy wrath — for thou, O god, dost mark all transgression; a hundred, a thousand others I drive away; let this man of ours live to see out the years.

sanskrit: yad uvakthānṛtaṃ jihvayā vṛjinaṃ bahu | rājñas tvā satyadharmaṇo muñcāmi varuṇād aham ||
english: Whatever untruth thou hast spoken with thy tongue, much that is crooked — I release thee from Varuṇa, the king whose ordinance is truth.

sanskrit: amuñcaṃ tvā vaiśvānarād arṇavān mahatas pari | sajātān ugra ā vada brahma cāpa cakīhi naḥ ||
english: I have released thee from Vaiśvānara, from beyond the great ocean-floods; speak forth, O fierce one, to thy kinsmen; fashion the sacred utterance and do homage for us.
